cohort.eligibilityRule: A product must have a public first-party page explicitly offering measurement, monitoring, benchmarking, or optimization of brand visibility, mentions, citations, or positioning in AI-generated search or answer systems.

eligibility.answerEligibleWhen: The provider call succeeds and returns at least one valid HTTP or HTTPS source URL.

matching.brandMention: Exact cohort alias match using Unicode letter-and-number boundaries. Case sensitivity follows each cohort row's match_policy.
matching.claimedDomainCitation: A normalized cited hostname exactly matches the claimed domain or is one of its subdomains.

prominence.lead: The brand is the first cohort brand mentioned in the answer.
prominence.shortlist: The brand is the second through fifth distinct cohort brand mentioned in the answer.
prominence.incidental: The brand is the sixth or later distinct cohort brand mentioned in the answer.
prominence.absent: No approved cohort alias is matched in the answer.

metrics.discoveryVisibility: Eligible discovery answers mentioning the brand divided by eligible discovery answers.
metrics.prominence: Mean registered prominence score across eligible discovery answers.
metrics.providerCoverage: Eligible answers divided by planned answers.
metrics.citationPresence: Eligible answers citing the brand's claimed domain divided by eligible answers.
metrics.sourceFrequency: Eligible answers citing each normalized source domain, counting a domain at most once per answer.

limitations: The study is a time-stamped API-grounded comparison and does not claim parity with consumer chat interfaces.
The registered questions are not a random or statistically representative sample of all buyer questions.
Brand prominence is an order-based proxy and does not prove recommendation strength.
A citation does not prove that the cited page caused a brand mention or recommendation.
The product cohort is a defined comparison set, not an exhaustive list or endorsement.
